title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts, make the recommit depth cap also count narrowing as a gene
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/feature-compose.ts, make the recommit depth cap also count narrowing as a generation, so the recommit/narrow alternation terminates.

WHY. Two guards each cap one direction of one loop and the alternation slips between them. The RECOMMIT DEPTH CAP refuses a new recommit gap once the id carries two "recommit-" prefixes. Separately, gap-to-feature's shouldNarrowForChronicFailure refuses to NARROW a gap that is already a recommit. Neither covers the other order: a root gap is narrowed to "<root>-narrowed", its compose fails, and a recommit is filed as "recommit-<root>-narrowed-<class>" — an id with exactly ONE "recommit-" prefix, which the cap reads as generation 1 and files freely. Measured in the live store: of 391 open recommit gaps, 154 carry a "-narrowed" segment with fewer than two "recommit-" prefixes, and 153 of those were minted AFTER the narrowing guard landed on 2026-08-30, so that guard demonstrably did not close this direction.

THE CHANGE. Exactly one op, on an executable statement. Find this line, which occurs exactly once in the file:

      if (reCommit && _recommitDepth < 2) {

Replace that single line with exactly this line:

      if (reCommit && _recommitDepth + (String(gap.id).match(/-narrowed/g) ?? []).length < 2) {

WHAT THIS CHANGES AT RUNTIME. This is NOT a cosmetic or declaration-only edit: it changes the branch condition that decides whether a substrateGap_write is executed. For an id such as "recommit-route-edit-d8528524-narrowed-semantic_reject" the left side becomes 1 + 1 = 2, the condition becomes false, and the gap is NOT filed — where today it IS filed. On the live store that flips 154 ids from filed to refused.

SCOPE. One replacement only, on that single if-statement line. Do not modify the "const _recommitDepth = ..." declaration above it, the gap body inside the branch, or the failure_lessons write. The threshold stays 2; only what counts as a generation changes, which is the intent the comment directly above already states — a gap that has been through two rounds of amplification is a PERSISTENT failure and should be dispositioned rather than re-filed. [RETRY CONTEXT — compose for gap route-edit-11f1b6ba repeated already-recorded failure class semantic_reject: The patch modifies the recommit depth cap condition to count both 'recommit-' prefixes and '-narrowed' segments, effectively closing the described loo. The specification is above; this failure text is context only and is not the specification.]
